settings.resources.batch_size.label: Repositories per batch

settings.group.updates.help: What happens to each kind of update: a pull request for you to merge, an automatic merge, a question first, or nothing. Applies to all repositories; a repository can still make exceptions in its own renovate.json.
settings.updates.major.label: Major updates
settings.updates.major.help: New versions that may break things, for example 1.x to 2.x.
settings.updates.minor.label: Minor updates
settings.updates.minor.help: New features that should stay compatible, for example 1.1 to 1.2.
settings.updates.patch.label: Patch updates
settings.updates.patch.help: Bug fixes and small changes, for example 1.1.1 to 1.1.2. Digests and pins follow this setting.
settings.updates.group_non_major.label: One pull request for minor and patch
settings.updates.group_non_major.help: Combines all minor and patch updates of a repository into a single pull request. Works best when both use the same action.
settings.updates.minimum_age_days.label: Wait after a release (days)
settings.updates.minimum_age_days.help: A version is offered only after it has been out this long, so broken releases are found by others first. 0 switches the wait off.
settings.updates.merge_method.label: Merge method
settings.updates.merge_method.help: How automatic merges are made. Automatic uses what the repository allows.
settings.updates.dashboard.label: Dependency Dashboard
settings.updates.dashboard.help: One issue per repository that lists all pending updates. Empty leaves it to the repository. It is always on while an action is set to "Ask me first".
settings.renovate.ignored_authors.label: Ignored commit authors
settings.renovate.ignored_authors.help: Commits by these authors do not count as manual edits. The default is the Mend Renovate app, so pull requests it opened can be taken over.
recipe.locked: These settings are fixed in the app configuration.
recipe.careful.name: Careful
recipe.careful.text: Every update arrives as a pull request. You look at each one and merge it yourself.
recipe.balanced.name: Balanced
recipe.balanced.text: Small updates merge by themselves once the checks are green. Major updates wait as a pull request for you. A release must be 3 days old first.
recipe.quiet.name: Quiet
recipe.quiet.text: As balanced, but all small updates share one pull request and major updates only show up when you tick them in the Dependency Dashboard.
recipe.hands_off.name: Hands off
recipe.hands_off.text: Everything merges by itself when the checks are green, major updates included. Only for repositories with good tests.

guide.title: Guide
guide.subtitle: How to get Renovate to do what you want. Short answers to the questions that come up first.
guide.start.title: Getting started in four steps
guide.start.step1: Connect your git server under Connections. Use a separate account for Renovate (see "Your own account").
guide.start.step2: Switch on the repositories Renovate should look after.
guide.start.step3: Choose what happens to updates (see "Which updates are merged automatically?"), or leave it to each repository.
guide.start.step4: Press "Run now". A run takes a few minutes; the Runs page shows what was found.
guide.start.onboarding: A repository without a Renovate configuration gets an onboarding pull request first. Merge it to start. A repository that already has a `renovate.json` (or `.github/renovate.json`) is used as it is.
guide.recipes.title: Which updates are merged automatically?
guide.recipes.intro: Every update has a kind: major (1.x to 2.x), minor (1.1 to 1.2) or patch (1.1.1 to 1.1.2). For each kind you choose one of these actions:
guide.recipes.repository: `As the repository decides`: the app adds nothing, the repository's own configuration applies. This is the default, so existing setups keep working.
guide.recipes.pr: `Pull request, I merge`: a pull request is opened and never merged by Renovate.
guide.recipes.approval: `Ask me first`: the update is only listed in the Dependency Dashboard issue of the repository. It gets its pull request when you tick it.
guide.recipes.automerge: `Merge automatically`: a pull request is opened and merged as soon as its checks are green.
guide.recipes.ignore: `Skip`: the update is not offered at all.
guide.recipes.where: The recipes above only fill in the options of Settings, Updates and merging. You can change every option there afterwards.
guide.recipes.checks: Renovate merges only when the checks of a pull request are green. A repository without any checks has nothing that can stop a bad update, so be careful with automatic merging there, and protect your default branch.
guide.recipes.exceptions: A repository can still make exceptions with its own rules, for example in its `renovate.json`. Rules written there win over the settings of the app:
guide.account.title: Your own account for commits, issues and pull requests
guide.account.intro: Everything Renovate does is done as the account behind the token: pull requests, issues, comments and commits. Give it its own account, for example `renovate-bot`, so your history stays clean and you can see at a glance what comes from Renovate.
guide.account.step1: Create the account on your git server. GitHub: a normal free account. GitLab, Gitea and Forgejo: a regular user.
guide.account.step2: Give it access to the repositories: add it as a collaborator with write access, or to an organization through a team with write access.
guide.account.step3: Sign in as that account, create an access token (see "Token permissions") and use it under Connections, Add connection. Not your own token.
guide.account.step4: Optional, only for the author of commits: Settings, Renovate, Commit author, for example `Renovate Bot <renovate-bot@example.org>`. Left empty, Renovate uses the name and address of the account. For GitHub to show the account's picture on commits, use its no-reply address `ID+USERNAME@users.noreply.github.com` (the ID is shown at `https://api.github.com/users/USERNAME`).
guide.account.note: Pull requests and issues always carry the name of the account behind the token. The commit author setting changes the commits only.
guide.token.title: Token permissions
guide.token.intro: The token must be allowed to push branches, open pull requests and write issues (for the Dependency Dashboard).
guide.token.github: GitHub, fine-grained token: select the repositories, then Contents, Pull requests, Issues, Workflows and Commit statuses on "Read and write", Checks on "Read and write", Metadata on "Read".
guide.token.github_classic: GitHub, classic token: the scope `repo`, and `workflow` if workflow files are updated.
guide.token.gitea: Gitea and Forgejo: read and write for Repository and Issue, read for User, Organization and Miscellaneous.
guide.token.others: Other servers: the setup assistant lists what is needed on its token page.
guide.token.symptom: Issues appear but no pull requests? The token usually lacks the permission for pull requests. Check it first.
guide.config.title: Configuring a repository
guide.config.intro: Renovate reads the configuration of a repository itself. Nothing has to be moved when you come from another Renovate.
guide.config.files: These places are looked at, in this order: `renovate.json`, `.github/renovate.json`, `.gitlab/renovate.json`, `.renovaterc`, `.renovaterc.json` and the key `renovate` in `package.json` (also as `.json5`).
guide.config.onboarding: Without such a file, the app opens an onboarding pull request with the preset from Settings, Renovate. Turn this off there if you do not want it.
guide.config.presets: Presets such as `github>owner/repo` are read from github.com (add a GitHub.com token under Settings, Renovate, to avoid rate limits). `local>owner/repo` reads from the same server as the repository.
guide.config.more: The full list of options is in the documentation of Renovate: https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/
guide.mend.title: Coming from the Mend Renovate app
guide.mend.intro: Moving from the free cloud app of Mend works, with three things to know:
guide.mend.uninstall: Uninstall the Mend app from the repositories (or the organization), or two bots work on the same branches.
guide.mend.edited: Pull requests of the old bot look "edited" to a new account because their commits have another author. This app ignores the commits of the Mend bot by default (Settings, Renovate, Ignored commit authors), so it takes them over. If a branch is still marked "Edited/Blocked" in the Dependency Dashboard, tick its rebase box, or close the pull request and delete the branch.
guide.mend.config: Your `renovate.json` stays where it is, for example `.github/renovate.json`.
guide.mend.onboarding: The onboarding pull request is not opened again for repositories that already have a configuration.
guide.nothing.title: Issues appear, but no pull requests?
guide.nothing.intro: Work through this list from the top. Open the latest run first: it says per repository why updates were held back.
guide.nothing.step1: Run details, repository: the yellow box names the reason, for example "changed by someone else", "waits for your approval" or "limit reached".
guide.nothing.step2: Token: does it have the permission for pull requests (see "Token permissions")? Without it issues work and pull requests fail.
guide.nothing.step3: Dry run: under Settings, Renovate it must be "Off". Otherwise Renovate only looks and changes nothing. A preview run never changes anything either.
guide.nothing.step4: Update actions: "Ask me first" shows an update only in the Dependency Dashboard issue until you tick it. "Skip" hides it.
guide.nothing.step5: Schedule in the repository: a `"schedule"` option in its renovate.json (for example "before 6am on monday") restricts when pull requests are opened. Outside that window every run only updates the Dependency Dashboard issue. Make the app run inside the window (Settings, Schedule), for example `0 4 * * 1`.
guide.nothing.step6: Limits: the number of open pull requests (default 10 per repository) and the wait after a release (Settings, Updates and merging).
guide.nothing.step7: Old pull requests of another bot: see "Coming from the Mend Renovate app".
guide.many.title: One setup for many repositories
guide.many.intro: With many repositories you do not want to repeat yourself. Three layers each have their own job, and the lower one wins:
guide.many.layer_app: **The app (Settings)**: who and how much. Commit author, labels, update actions and recipes, limits, onboarding, tokens for registries, and when Renovate runs. Applies to every repository.
guide.many.layer_preset: **A shared preset**: what is updated and how. Package rules, grouping, version rules and custom managers that all your repositories share. Keep it in one repository (for example `owner/renovate-config` with a `default.json`) and name it under Settings, Renovate, Default presets as `github>owner/renovate-config` (on your own server `local>owner/renovate-config`). Every repository then uses it without a line of its own.
guide.many.layer_repo: **The repository's own file**: only the exceptions of that project, in its `renovate.json`. It can be nearly empty.
guide.many.copy: Alternative: every repository carries a full copy of the shared file, kept in step by a script. That works with private presets too, but a change has to reach every repository.
guide.many.settings_title: Recommended settings for a setup like this:
guide.many.s_config: Require configuration: `required`, so only repositories that carry a Renovate file are touched. Switch the onboarding pull request off if all of them have one.
guide.many.s_account: A dedicated account and a commit author, see "Your own account".
guide.many.s_updates: Update actions: the recipe "Balanced", or your own choice per kind of update.
guide.many.s_limits: Open pull requests at once: 6 to 10. New pull requests per hour: 0 (no limit), because the runs are hours apart anyway.
guide.many.s_schedule: Schedule: pick when Renovate runs (Settings, Schedule) and do not restrict it a second time in every repository. If a repository does say `"schedule": ["before 6am on monday"]`, the app has to run inside that window, for example `0 4 * * 1`, or pull requests never appear.
guide.many.s_token: A GitHub.com token under Settings, Renovate: release notes in the pull requests and no rate limits, also for repositories on other servers.
